citations.claim: energy exceeds allowed 4389.39 at first violating step
body 1 after floor bounce with high speed, energy already rising to 4217

counterfactual.change: Changed body 1 restitution e from 0.9 to 0.0 - removes energy gain on floor impact, preventing energy_bound violation

explanation: Body 1 hits floor with high restitution e=0.9 between step 0 and 1. Speed goes from 51.14 to 48.3 but energy increases from 3985 to 4217 then to 4565 at step 2, exceeding allowed 4389. The floor bounce with e=0.9 is not dissipating enough energy and combined with integration error/gravity handling adds energy. Changing e to 0.0 removes violation, confirming restitution-driven energy gain is cause.
vision_note: In tile 0 the lower ball is airborne above the floor, in tile 1 it appears to contact the floor, and in tile 2 it is slightly lifted again after the bounce while the upper ball remains largely stationary. No obvious tunneling or wall penetration is visible; the only distinct event is the floor impact and rebound of the lower body between steps 0 and 2.
